entity.name: Walt Disney
entity.description: The animator who built a magic kingdom from a bankrupt cartoon studio. Won 22 Academy Awards (still the individual record), created Mickey Mouse after losing his first cartoon character, and opened Disneyland when Hollywood thought theme parks were insane. Died of lung cancer before Disney World opened.

story.name: Walt Disney
story.description: Goes bankrupt in Kansas City, loses his first cartoon character to a distributor, creates Mickey Mouse on a train ride, premieres Snow White to a standing ovation, and builds Disneyland in an Anaheim orange grove.

moments.name: Walt Disney Is Born in Chicago's Hermosa Neighborhood
moments.subtitle: The fourth son of a struggling carpenter who will become America's most famous entertainer
moments.description: On December 5, 1901, Walter Elias Disney was born at 1249 Tripp Avenue in Chicago's Hermosa neighborhood. His father Elias Disney had emigrated from Canada; his mother Flora was of German and English descent. When Walt was four, the family moved to a farm in Marceline, Missouri, where Disney developed his love of drawing. He was paid to sketch a retired neighbor's horse, his first artistic commission. Disney later described Marceline as the happiest period of his childhood and drew inspiration from the small town for decades of future work, including the Main Street USA concept at Disneyland.

moments.name: Walt Disney's First Animation Studio Goes Bankrupt in Kansas City
moments.subtitle: A 21-year-old animator loses everything but gains the skills that will change entertainment forever
moments.description: In 1923, Walt Disney's Laugh-O-Gram Studio in Kansas City, Missouri, went bankrupt. Disney had founded the studio in May 1921 after his short cartoon films for a local theater proved popular. He hired animators including Ub Iwerks, Rudolf Ising, and Hugh Harman, but the cartoons did not generate enough revenue to sustain the business. Disney had begun production on Alice's Wonderland, combining live action with animation, but completed it too late to save the company. Broke and just 21 years old, Disney packed up and moved to Hollywood in July 1923. Within five years, he would create Mickey Mouse.

moments.name: Disney and Iwerks Create Mickey Mouse After Losing Oswald the Rabbit
moments.subtitle: Betrayed by a distributor who stole his cartoon character, Disney invents a replacement that conquers the world
moments.description: In early 1928, Walt Disney traveled to New York to negotiate a larger budget for his successful Oswald the Lucky Rabbit cartoon series, only to discover that distributor Charles Mintz had secretly hired away most of his animators and that Universal Pictures owned the character's rights. Betrayed and nearly staffless, Disney returned to Los Angeles and, with his loyal animator Ub Iwerks, created a new character: Mickey Mouse. Disney's wife Lillian talked him out of the original name 'Mortimer Mouse.' The first Mickey cartoon with synchronized sound, Steamboat Willie, premiered on November 18, 1928, and became a sensation.

moments.name: Disneyland Opens in an Anaheim Orange Grove and Reinvents Entertainment
moments.subtitle: Hollywood thought it was insane, but 28,000 people showed up on opening day
moments.description: On July 17, 1955, Disneyland opened in Anaheim, California, on 160 acres of former orange groves. Walt Disney had spent years developing the concept of a clean, story-driven theme park, a radical departure from the seedy carnivals of the era. Opening day, broadcast live on ABC television, was a notorious disaster dubbed 'Black Sunday': temperatures hit 101 degrees, rides broke down, and counterfeit tickets doubled the expected crowd to 28,000. Despite the chaotic debut, Disneyland attracted one million visitors in its first seven weeks. It launched the modern theme park industry and remains one of the most visited places on Earth.

moments.name: Walt Disney Dies of Lung Cancer at 65 Before Disney World Opens
moments.subtitle: A lifelong heavy smoker, Disney never sees his most ambitious project completed
moments.description: On December 15, 1966, Walt Disney died of circulatory collapse caused by lung cancer at St. Joseph Hospital in Burbank, California. He was 65 years old. A heavy smoker throughout his life, Disney had been diagnosed with cancer just weeks earlier after a spot was found on his lung during an X-ray. At the time of his death, he was deep in planning for Disney World in Florida, centered on his utopian vision of a planned city called EPCOT (Experimental Prototype Community of Tomorrow). Disney World opened in 1971 without him. His company grew to become one of the world's largest media conglomerates, worth over $200 billion.
